outcome: Operator-facing refusals stop discarding the reason they refused: writeCommandFailure and writeKnownFailure render the raising error's own text (bounded, secret-free) beneath the fixed fallback sentence and Technical code, gitx.Error's Op (the git args) and Err (the stderr/timeout tail) reach the operator for GIT_EXECUTION_FAILED, baton.RecordError.Msg reaches the operator for INVALID_FIELD/INVALID_PATH/INVALID_PLAN_FENCE with INVALID_PATH naming which canonicalization rule failed and the offending value's actual length when it hits the 512 bound, and driver's NATIVE_NOT_CERTIFIED/INVALID_ADAPTER carry a Detail drawn from the 19-term closed vocabulary A4 enumerates (one term per independently-reachable validateNativeConfig/validatePinnedRuntimeFiles/NewNativeAdapter condition, covering cli identity, admission bounds, pin mode, credential target, version, version output, digest, family, runtime-file presence/shape/digest/duplicate/missing, trust anchor, toolchain root, and NewNativeAdapter's own key/id/version/resolver checks), surfaced by the doctor registry-build path and by init's admission messages - closing sworn#254 (INVALID_PLAN discarded the error that caused it), sworn#273 (GIT_EXECUTION_FAILED printed with no cause), and the sworn#267 residual (INVALID_ADAPTER/NATIVE_NOT_CERTIFIED name no condition). Today commandErrorCode (cmd/sworn/main.go:1094-1120) does errors.As against every one of these error types and returns only .Code; writeCommandFailure (main.go:1055-1092) never prints err.Error(), .Op, .Err, .Msg, or .Detail; writeKnownFailure (main.go:1038-1053) never touches an error at all - so every refusal beneath these codes reads identically regardless of which raise site actually fired: internal/gitx/repository.go:499, internal/baton/plan.go (:133, :143, :760, :1404, :1409, :1413) and plan_authoring.go (:43, :274), and internal/driver/native.go (:173-182 NewNativeAdapter's own four checks folding into INVALID_ADAPTER, :214-280 validateNativeConfig's eleven OR-bundled raise sites, and :311-358 validatePinnedRuntimeFiles's further sub-conditions reached through :261-268).

exclude: internal/gitx package code itself is not touched: gitx.Error's Op and Err fields are already exported (repository.go:42-47) and populated at the GIT_EXECUTION_FAILED raise site (repository.go:499); this slice only makes cmd/sworn read fields that already exist.

the writeCommandFailure switch's existing custom messages for OWNER_TRANSITION_PENDING, APPROVAL_PENDING, RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN, EFFECT_PARKED, RUN_NOT_FOUND/INVALID_RUN, BATON_UNAVAILABLE, and GIT_UNAVAILABLE (main.go:1063-1087) stay exactly as they are; this slice adds detail beneath the fallback sentence for the remaining codes, it does not touch this switch.

the driver provider-status Detail pattern (PROVIDER_LIMITED, PROVIDER_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED, PROVIDER_REQUEST_REJECTED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, PROVIDER_ERROR, PROVIDER_TRANSPORT_FAILED) and NATIVE_SURFACE_INVALID/PROCESS_START_FAILED's own structured envelopes, all funneled through normalizeAdapterError (invoke.go:536) and bounded at maxProviderErrorDetailBytes (pacing.go:73), already carry Detail and are untouched; this slice only adds Detail where none exists today.

internal/journal, internal/cockpit, and internal/runtime error types (journal.Error, cockpit.Error, runtimepkg.Error) keep surfacing only .Code through commandErrorCode; the brief scopes detail-rendering to gitx, baton, and driver refusals only, so no fields are added to those three other packages.

every default value, validation rule, and Technical code stays exactly what it is today; this slice only makes an already-computed reason reach stderr, it introduces no new terminal code and relaxes no admission rule.

strictjson.go's asString/requiredString generic bound message (strictjson.go:252-258) is unchanged for every caller except repositoryPath; other INVALID_FIELD bound violations elsewhere in internal/baton keep today's message exactly.

the boolean conditions each validateNativeConfig/validatePinnedRuntimeFiles admission rule tests do not change; A4 only requires enough branch-splitting to attach the specified closed-vocabulary term to each named group, never a change to which configs pass or fail.

acceptance.text: writeCommandFailure and writeKnownFailure render the underlying error's own text (bounded, secret-free) beneath the fixed fallback sentence and 'Technical code: %s' line, for every wrapped error type this slice touches - gitx, baton, and driver alike - not just one representative case. Today writeKnownFailure (main.go:1038-1053) prints only its caller-supplied message and code string and never touches an error; writeCommandFailure (main.go:1055-1092) computes code := commandErrorCode(err) at :1061, its switch at :1063-1087 crafts custom prose for exactly OWNER_TRANSITION_PENDING/APPROVAL_PENDING/RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN/EFFECT_PARKED/RUN_NOT_FOUND,INVALID_RUN/BATON_UNAVAILABLE/GIT_UNAVAILABLE and otherwise keeps the caller's fallback string verbatim, printing at :1088-1091 without ever calling err.Error(); commandErrorCode (main.go:1094-1120) does errors.As against *runtimepkg.Error, *gitx.Error, *journal.Error, *driver.ContractError, *cockpit.Error, *baton.RecordError and returns only .Code, reading none of .Op/.Err/.Msg/.Detail/.Paths - so baton.RecordError.Msg is silently dropped today at every one of plan_command.go's three writeCommandFailure call sites: plan pin (call :66, failure at :71-72 'Could not pin the manifest.'), plan lint (call :99, failure at :104-105 'Scope lint failed.'), plan record (call :178, failure at :184-185 'Could not record the plan revision.'), even though RecordError.Error() (strictjson.go:35-40) already formats Code+': '+Msg(+': '+Err.Error() when Err != nil) ready to be read; raise sites feeding these three commands include ParsePlan's INVALID_PLAN_FENCE (plan.go:133, :143) and PinManifest/RunPlanScopeLint's own INVALID_PLAN_FENCE (plan_authoring.go:43, :274). The existing switch's custom messages and the codes commandErrorCode returns do not change. Pinned by a cmd/sworn unit test asserting writeCommandFailure's output contains a gitx and a driver error's own detail text beneath the Technical code line for a code outside the existing switch, plus a cmd/sworn test invoking plan pin, plan lint, and plan record each against a fixture that fails with a known RecordError, asserting the printed output contains that error's Msg text.

GIT_EXECUTION_FAILED shows which git invocation ran and why it failed. gitx.Error (internal/gitx/repository.go:42-47: Code, Op, Err, Paths, TotalPaths) is raised at repository.go:499 as fail("GIT_EXECUTION_FAILED", strings.Join(args, " "), errors.New(message)), where message is built from stderr/wait-error/timeout/overflow text at :486-498, and Error() (:49-54) already formats Code+': '+Op+': '+Err.Error() - but no cmd/sworn caller reads Op or Err, since commandErrorCode discards them at main.go:1099-1102 and keeps only Code. After this slice, a git failure reaching the operator through writeCommandFailure or writeKnownFailure prints the git args and the stderr-derived failure text, not just the bare code. Pinned by a cmd/sworn test that drives a git operation to GIT_EXECUTION_FAILED and asserts the printed output contains both the joined args and the stderr-derived text.

repositoryPath (internal/baton/plan.go:1396-1416) names which canonicalization rule failed instead of printing the identical 'label is not a canonical repository path' string at all three of its rejection sites - :1404 (leading/trailing slash, an embedded backslash, or a control character), :1409 (an empty, '.', or '..' path segment), :1413 (a literal '.git' first segment) - and for a value over the 512-rune bound, rejected earlier at requiredString(value,label,1,512) (:1397 delegating to asString, strictjson.go:252-258), reports the offending value's actual rune length itself, since asString's returned message states only the bound ('%s must be a string of %d-%d characters') and never the actual length. repositoryPath is reached from scope.include (plan.go:984) and scope.exclude (plan.go:999) via uniqueStringList, and directly from package (:1153), contract_path (:1245), and touchpoints (:1267) - every caller inherits the fix with no change at the call sites. This criterion is internal/baton-only and independent of A1: A1 pins that writeCommandFailure/plan_command.go surface whatever Msg repositoryPath already returns; this pins that the Msg repositoryPath returns is itself rule- and length-specific. Pinned by internal/baton unit tests calling repositoryPath directly: one case per canonicalization rule (three) plus the over-512 case, each asserting the returned error's Msg is rule- or length-specific rather than the one shared string today.

driver's NATIVE_NOT_CERTIFIED and INVALID_ADAPTER carry a Detail naming which of a closed, fully-enumerated set of admission conditions failed, not an open-ended name a worker invents: every independently-reachable failure below gets a fixed term, with sharing stated explicitly wherever one line's OR bundles conditions too fine-grained for an operator to act on differently, and NewNativeAdapter's own four pre-validateNativeConfig checks are explicitly in scope with their own terms - resolving whether the INVALID_ADAPTER collapse covers them. Closed vocabulary, 19 terms: validateNativeConfig (native.go:214-280) - cli_identity (validateExecutableIdentity failure, split out of the :215-218 OR into its own branch); cli_admission_bounds (the remaining :216-217 sub-conditions - credential-byte lower bound, upper bound, version-output empty, version-output oversized - share this term); pin_mode (:226-227); credential_target (:231-232 codex, :245-246 claude, :261-262 credential-target not absolute/not clean - three sites share, all naming the same operator fact); version (declared-version mismatch half of :235-237 codex-minor and :249-251 claude-minor, plus :239 codex-exact CLIVersion and :253 claude-exact CLIVersion - four sites share); version_output (the VersionOutput-string half of those same four sites: :236-237, :241-242, :250-251, :255-256); digest (:240 codex CLI.Digest, :254 claude CLI.Digest); family (:259 unknown Family); toolchain_root (:270-276). validatePinnedRuntimeFiles (native.go:311-358, reached through the :261-268 OR's validatePinnedRuntimeFiles call) - runtime_file (:316-318, nothing pinned); runtime_file_shape (:321-331's malformed-path/target and guest-workspace/home/sworn-collision sub-conditions, excluding digest); runtime_file_digest (:325 bad per-file digest, split out of the :321-331 OR); runtime_file_duplicate (:332-334 duplicate target, :338-341 duplicate required target - share); runtime_file_missing (:343-345 a declared-required target absent); trust_anchor (:347-355, any of the four well-known cert/resolv/hosts/nsswitch files absent - share). NewNativeAdapter (native.go:173-182) - adapter_key (:177 providerKeyPattern mismatch), adapter_id (:178 driverIdentityPattern mismatch), adapter_version (:179 versionPattern mismatch), credential_resolver (:180 resolver == nil). Today contract.go:165's fail(code) sets no Detail, so all of these collapse to bare NATIVE_NOT_CERTIFIED or INVALID_ADAPTER with ContractError.Detail (contract.go:109) always empty. After this slice, fail gains a Detail-carrying sibling (mirroring failContinuation, contract.go:167-169); each site above sets its listed term; validateNativeConfig forwards validatePinnedRuntimeFiles's Detail at :268 instead of discarding it behind its own bare fail; and NewNativeAdapter's :181 fold forwards whichever Detail actually fired - its own four checks' term, or validateNativeConfig's forwarded term - instead of re-wrapping bare INVALID_ADAPTER. init's admission round-trip (init_command.go:907-918, code read at :916, and :944 for EncodeDriverConfig) and the doctor/inspect/certify registry-build failure (driver.go:71-84, writeCommandFailure at :82) both print it. Pinned by internal/driver unit tests, one assertion per term above (19 cases) driving the exact triggering input and asserting that exact Detail string, plus a cmd/sworn test over buildDriverConfig / the doctor command asserting the printed message names the failed condition.

constraints: Every Technical code stays exactly what it is today: NATIVE_NOT_CERTIFIED and INVALID_ADAPTER keep their .Code, gaining only a populated .Detail; no code in commandErrorCode's vocabulary is added, renamed, or removed, and the codes-only tests at main_test.go:449-511 keep passing unmodified.

Every rendered string is bounded and secret-free: git stderr/args, baton Msg text, and driver Detail must never carry credential bytes, tokens, or unbounded command output at the operator surface; driver's new Detail values are drawn only from A4's fixed 19-term closed vocabulary constructed inside internal/driver (mirroring failContinuation, contract.go:167-169), never provider or credential bytes, so they need no normalizeAdapterError funnel re-validation.

This is additive text beneath an unchanged fallback sentence and Technical code line, never a replacement of either; a test asserting on today's fallback sentence or on a Contains("Technical code: X") check keeps passing.

The repositoryPath canonicalization rules themselves, and every validateNativeConfig/validatePinnedRuntimeFiles admission rule - which values are rejected - do not change; only the message or Detail accompanying an existing rejection gains specificity.

The provider-status Detail funnel (normalizeAdapterError, invoke.go:536) and its bound (maxProviderErrorDetailBytes, pacing.go:73) are reused conceptually but not modified; NATIVE_NOT_CERTIFIED/INVALID_ADAPTER Detail is same-process closed-vocabulary text and stays outside that funnel, matching CONTINUATION_INVALID's existing treatment.
